title: System Design Fundamentals
description: Practical system design reference covering requirements, capacity estimation, APIs, decomposition, data modeling, caching, load balancing, partitioning, replication, consistency, transactions, messaging, resilience, security, observability, deployment, and design review.

subtopics.title: Functional & Quality Requirements
subtopics.description: Start with user-visible capabilities and invariants, then quantify availability, durability, latency, throughput, consistency, recovery, security, compliance, cost, and operability.

codeBlocks.code:
Functional: create order, pay, query status, cancel under policy
Invariant: one captured payment per accepted idempotency key
SLO: 99.9% successful API availability; p99 read < 300 ms
Durability: acknowledged order loss < defined target
Recovery: RPO 5 min, RTO 30 min
Constraints: regions, data residency, team skills, budget, deadlines

callouts.title: Avoid Designing from Technology Names
callouts.text: A requirement like 'must use Kafka' hides the actual need. State ordering, replay, fan-out, throughput, retention, and failure behavior first.

subtopics.title: Capacity & Back-of-the-Envelope Estimation
subtopics.description: Estimate average and peak requests, records, bytes, retention, fan-out, concurrency, connections, bandwidth, storage, growth, and failure/recovery headroom.

codeBlocks.code:
Daily writes = writes/sec × 86,400
Raw storage = records × avg bytes × retention
Provisioned storage ≈ raw × indexes/overhead × replicas × safety factor
Concurrency ≈ arrival rate × average time in system
Peak capacity = measured/estimated peak × failover headroom
Always record assumptions and sensitivity ranges

callouts.title: Average Capacity Hides Bursts
callouts.text: Model diurnal peaks, launches, retries, batch jobs, hot keys, zone loss, replica catch-up, reindexing, backups, and organic growth.

subtopics.title: APIs, Data Flow & Trust Boundaries
subtopics.description: Draw actors, synchronous calls, asynchronous events, stores, caches, external dependencies, administrative paths, and trust boundaries before optimizing components.

diagram.content:
flowchart LR
  Client --> Edge["Edge / API boundary"]
  Edge --> Service["Domain service"]
  Service --> DB["Authoritative store"]
  Service --> Outbox["Transactional outbox"]
  Outbox --> Broker["Event broker"]
  Broker --> Workers["Consumers"]
  Workers --> Search["Derived search index"]

callouts.title: Mark the Source of Truth
callouts.text: Every derived cache, index, stream, and read model needs rebuild, freshness, reconciliation, and outage behavior relative to authoritative state.

subtopics.title: Load Balancing & Horizontal Scaling
subtopics.description: Distribute stateless work across healthy instances, externalize durable state, drain during deployment, and understand whether affinity is required or hiding poor state ownership.

codeBlocks.code:
DNS/global routing → regional load balancer → service instances
Health: startup, readiness, liveness answer different questions
Scale signal: user latency/queue depth/concurrency, not CPU alone
Drain: stop new traffic → finish bounded work → close resources
Downstream: pool/concurrency limits prevent scale-out overload

callouts.title: Autoscaling Can Move the Bottleneck
callouts.text: More application replicas can exhaust databases, brokers, third-party quotas, NAT ports, or connection limits. Scale the whole dependency chain or apply backpressure.

subtopics.title: Data Modeling, Indexes & Partitioning
subtopics.description: Model invariants and access patterns first. Index reads deliberately, then partition by a key that distributes load while preserving necessary locality and transaction scope.

callouts.title: Partition Keys Become Architecture
callouts.text: They affect transactions, joins, migrations, hot spots, routing, resharding, and failure domains. Measure skew and plan movement before scale forces it.

subtopics.title: Caching, CDNs & Invalidation
subtopics.description: Cache derived values at browser, CDN, gateway, service, or datastore layers only with explicit key, TTL, freshness, invalidation, authorization, stampede, and fallback semantics.

codeBlocks.code:
Cache-aside read: GET → miss → authoritative read → SET ttl+jitter
Write: commit source of truth → invalidate/update after commit
Stampede: request coalescing, stale-while-revalidate, bounded refresh
Failure: decide fail-open stale, fail-closed, or bypass per data class

callouts.title: Cache Keys Include Every Result Dimension
callouts.text: Tenant, identity/authorization, locale, currency, feature flags, version, query, and representation can change results. Missing dimensions cause correctness or data leaks.

subtopics.title: Replication & Consistency Models
subtopics.description: Replication improves read scale and availability but introduces lag, conflicts, failover ambiguity, and durability trade-offs. State guarantees per operation rather than labeling a whole system simply consistent or available.

rows: Operations appear atomic in real time
Observed state does not go backward

callouts.title: Replica Read Can Violate User Expectations
callouts.text: After a write, route to primary, use session/version tokens, wait for a replica position, or communicate pending state where read-your-writes matters.

subtopics.title: Transactions, Sagas & Transactional Outbox
subtopics.description: Keep strong invariants inside one transactional authority when possible. Across services, coordinate steps with idempotency, durable state, retries, and compensations rather than pretending there is one atomic commit.

codeBlocks.code:
Local transaction: domain update + outbox record commit together
Relay: publish outbox event with stable ID; mark/retain progress
Consumer: deduplicate/inbox + local transaction + effect
Saga: persisted step state + retry policy + semantic compensation
Reconciliation: compare authorities and repair incomplete workflows

callouts.title: Compensation Is Not Time Reversal
callouts.text: Refunding a payment, releasing inventory, or sending a correction has new failure modes and audit meaning. Design it as a first-class operation.

subtopics.title: Queues, Logs, Delivery & Backpressure
subtopics.description: Choose queues for work distribution and logs/streams for retained ordered history and replay. Define delivery, ordering, retry, poison, retention, and consumer progress semantics.

codeBlocks.code:
At-least-once is common → idempotent effect + stable message ID
Ordering scope → partition/key or single queue; never assume global order
Backpressure → bounded queue/prefetch/concurrency + upstream shed/slow
Poison → classify, bounded delay retry, quarantine, alert, replay
Schema → compatible evolution and ownership

callouts.title: A Broker Does Not Remove Coupling
callouts.text: It changes coupling to schemas, timing, ordering, retention, delivery, and operational dependencies. Consumers still need contract governance and coordinated semantic evolution.

subtopics.title: Timeouts, Retries, Circuit Breaking & Load Shedding
subtopics.description: Assume partial failure. Bound every wait and queue, propagate deadlines, retry only transient idempotent work with jitter, isolate resources, and shed optional load before collapse.

codeBlocks.code:
Deadline budget: edge 2s → service 1.7s → datastore 1.2s
Retry: one owning layer, max attempts, backoff+jitter, remaining budget
Bulkhead: separate pools/concurrency for critical vs batch
Circuit/load shed: reject quickly under known dependency or capacity failure
Fallback: stale/degraded only when semantically safe

callouts.title: Retries Multiply Across Layers
callouts.text: Three attempts at three nested layers can create 27 downstream calls. Coordinate retry ownership and expose attempt/load signals.

subtopics.title: Security & Observability by Design
subtopics.description: Map trust boundaries, minimize privileges and data, protect secrets, encrypt traffic, audit decisions, and emit metrics/logs/traces tied to user outcomes and deploys.

codeBlocks.code:
Security: identity → authorization → validation → least privilege → audit
Metrics: traffic, errors, latency, saturation + business outcomes
Logs: structured safe events with request/trace IDs
Traces: cross-service critical paths and dependencies
SLOs: user-visible indicators + multi-window burn alerts
Never put tokens, secrets, or raw sensitive payloads in telemetry

callouts.title: Observability Has a Cardinality Budget
callouts.text: Raw URLs, user IDs, request IDs, and error messages can overwhelm metric systems. Use bounded dimensions and controlled logs/traces for high-cardinality investigation.

subtopics.title: Design Review & Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Make assumptions, decisions, alternatives, failure modes, ownership, migrations, and validation explicit so the design can be challenged and operated.

codeBlocks.code:
□ Requirements/invariants/SLO/RPO/RTO and exclusions are quantified
□ Capacity assumptions and peak/failure headroom are recorded
□ Source of truth, schemas, consistency and partitioning are explicit
□ Timeouts, retries, idempotency, backpressure and overload behavior align
□ Security/privacy/threat model and tenant isolation are reviewed
□ Deploy, migration, rollback, backup/restore and disaster drills exist
□ SLOs, telemetry, alerts, runbooks and owners are assigned
□ Simplest viable design and rejected alternatives are documented

callouts.title: Production Checklist
callouts.text: Design from requirements, measure before scaling, keep strong invariants local, bound every resource, expect duplicates and partial failure, protect trust boundaries, prove recovery, instrument user outcomes, and revisit assumptions with production evidence.
